To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protoplasts from the sheath cells of the young non- photosynthetic leaves of Posidonia oceanic a, a seagrasses endemic of the Mediterranean Sea, express an outward rectifying K + channel that is permeable to K +, but not to Na + or other monovalent cation and an inward rectifying channel that is permeant to K +, impermeant to Na + and reversibly blocked by TEA + and La 3+.

Posidonia protoplasts possess at least three ion channels that are permeable to potassium and that the characteristics of the channels identified in the protoplast membranes of the seagrass Pos. oceanica are comparable with those identified in other halophytic and terrestrial plants.

Posidonia oceanicaplasmalemma contains at least three types of ion channels: an outward-rectifier that is permeable to potassium and impermeant to sodium, an inward rectifier that is selective for potassium, a channel permeable to all cations tested.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of ion channels in protoplasts from the Mediterranean seagrasses Posidonia oceanic, a plant that lives in a highly stressful environment and that is threatened by the effects of pollution and climate change.
the identification of the properties of ion transport systems in the protoplast of the seagrass P. oceanica.
the identification and properties of potassium channels and the characterization of a non-selective channel in the protoplast plasma membranes of P. oceanica.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ion channel properties identified in Posidonia are not unique and are not significantly different from those found in the plasma membrane of other halophytes.

the properties of ion transporters of Posidonia are very similar to those found in halophytes, suggesting that the seagrass is a halophytic plant, and that the ion transport systems are well adapted to the high osmotic pressure of the seawater.
Posidonia channels are similar to those of other plants, but with some peculiarities that are probably due to the peculiar environmental conditions of Posidonia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the channels identified in the protoplast of Posidonia sheath cells are similar to the channels identified in terrestrial and other halophyte plants.

the ion channel characteristics identified in P. oceanicaplasmalemma protoplasts are consistent with a role in the maintenance of turgor and the control of ion transport in this seagrass. © 2011 Elsevier GmbH.
Posidonia ion channels are very similar to those found in terrestrial plants, but they have a lower selectivity for potassium.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Posidonia has ion channels with similar properties to channels found in terrestrial plants, and in this respect, Posidonia is different from the halophytic seagrass Zostera marina, which is the only other seagrass whose channel properties are known.
P. oceanica shares with other plants a number of K + channels, but also has some unique features that may contribute to its adaptation to its peculiar environment.

the ion channels identified in the protoplast of P. oceanica are similar to those described in other halophytes and terrestrial plants, and are probably important in regulating the ionic balance of the cell.
